correctness.rationale: For an ordinary nonempty family the local existential containment and universal intersection tests on U_t have thresholds max(min A) and min(max A), respectively. The empty family gives (-1,n); a family containing the empty set gives (n,-1). Every ordinary pair is realized by one set when b≤d or two singleton sets otherwise, preserving the empty-family prefix. Global thresholds are suffix minima, and are recovered by testing all upsets; equality on atoms under every hereditary valuation implies equality of operators, and the converse follows by formula induction. In the nonempty suffix the last family containing the empty set gives D identically -1 and B ending at n. Otherwise a -1 to ordinary D transition can only be made by the last occurrence of a local empty subset; its local b=n forces the consecutive B's equal. Conversely put the family {∅} exactly at this transition and use ordinary local representatives elsewhere in the nonempty suffix. Thus no other compatibility constraint is needed. Weak-sequence counts and hockey-stick give the asserted sum without overcounting the distinguishable empty prefixes. The top signature (n-1,0) proves sharpness for n≥2; for n=1 the sole ordinary signature needs only one member. Independent enumeration of all local signature assignments on continual chains through n=4 agrees (3,22,224,2634); direct formula evaluation agrees through n=8. These finite checks supplement the proof, and the uploaded checker was inspected, not executed.
